meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero from a phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I'm waiting, Hale. Who entered that zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an explanation of who entered it and whether Owen was heard first. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position; she agreed to nothing and still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to know who decided and whether Owen was heard first.
What moved her: nothing, because the meeting ended before Hale gave her anything to weigh.
What cost ground: nothing in particular, though answering her direct question with a pleasantry gave her nothing and kept her pressing.
Try next time: when she asks who decided and on what basis, open with one plain sentence owning that the zero went in before her family was called, then put a dated document about Owen's own work in front of her.
